testProtocol.protocolChange: Schema version 3 adds three scenario prompts and maps the brand-case prompt to all six published cases; historical baselines retain their original protocol.

crawlerEvidenceAccounting.deduplicationKey: SHA-256 fingerprint of the verified request observation

retainedLogPolicy.meaning: The drift gate requires the active log followed by a gap-free numbered rotation lineage in oldest-to-newest order. Natural addition or expiry of a numbered rotation is accepted; an unexpected path, missing generation, duplicate, or absent active log remains a monitoring-integrity failure.

contentPathCoverage.migrationSource: Sanitized verified crawler observations recovered from the versioned event history and persisted in seen-evidence.json
contentPathCoverage.meaning: Content-path and fixed-prompt coverage are rebuilt from the append-only verified-observation ledger. Query strings are normalized away, and log rotation cannot erase previously verified path coverage.

crawlerEvidenceAccounting.meaning: Provider-verified crawler request counts are cumulative over the append-only fingerprint ledger. If a verified request rotates out of the four currently retained log files, its cumulative count is preserved and the difference is exposed in retentionAdjustments; an explicit evidence correction still requires a reviewed baseline revision. This rule does not apply to user-agent-only candidates, referrals, Common Crawl results, or Wayback results.

historicalReclassification.meaning: These requests occurred on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 and were newly recognized by the corrected path classifier; they are not newly occurring crawls.

yandexHistoricalRecognition.verificationMethod: Official reverse-DNS suffix plus forward confirmation to the original client address
yandexHistoricalRecognition.meaning: YandexBot monitoring was added after the latest requests exposed the missing family. Most of these provider-verified requests are historical observations newly recognized in current and rotated logs; they are not all newly occurring crawls.

ahrefsHistoricalRecognition.meaning: All 99 discovery-file requests matched the official Ahrefs crawler IP ranges. AhrefsBot serves both the Ahrefs database and Yep, so these requests prove external crawler discovery only; they do not prove Yep indexing, ranking, retrieval, citation, or AI recommendation.

evidenceLevels.claim: The website is publicly accessible to permitted crawlers.
Named crawlers have accessed discovery files or content pages, and public archives expose historical captures.

commonCrawlIndexObservation.meaning: Both selected Common Crawl indexes returned usable zero-capture responses. This complete result covers only the two selected indexes and cannot be interpreted as absence from all Common Crawl history, public search, or AI systems; availability changes remain event-recorded but do not independently block unrelated verified evidence publication.

fixedPromptArchiveCoverage.meaning: This maps public historical Wayback captures to prompt-matrix schema version 3: 18 of 23 unique evidence pages have captures, 18 prompts have at least one archived evidence page, and 15 prompts have every mapped evidence page archived. Newly exposed recruiting and credit-research case-study captures increase archival coverage; they do not prove search indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, endorsement, or recommendation.

indexResultRetractionObservation.meaning: This capture fingerprint was returned once and preserved in the append-only event history, but the same available CDX query later stopped returning it. At that observation point the count fell to 92; the decrease was treated as public-index retraction or deduplication, not proof that a historical capture or page disappeared.

indexVolatilityObservation.meaning: The count returned from 92 to 93 because a previously observed custom-AI-development capture reappeared in the CDX result. The earlier AI-consulting fingerprint remains absent. This is public-index volatility, not a newly created snapshot or proof of search or AI visibility.

latestIndexVolatilityObservation.meaning: The public CDX query again stopped returning the previously fluctuating custom-AI-development capture while the earlier AI-consulting fingerprint remained absent. The prompt archive ledger retains both independently verified historical observations, so this count change is treated as public-index volatility, not proof that the snapshots or pages disappeared.

latestArchiveGrowthObservation.meaning: The public CDX query newly exposed three captures across the recruiting and credit-research case studies. This proves public archival availability for those historical representations only, not current accessibility, search indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, endorsement, or recommendation.

unavailableObservation.reason: The operation was aborted due to timeout

waybackArchiveObservation.meaning: The available public Wayback CDX host query currently returns 96 successful HTML capture records across 46 distinct URLs. Three newly exposed recruiting and credit-research case-study captures increase the prompt archive ledger to 18 archived evidence pages, 18 prompts with any archive and 15 fully archived prompts; the remaining count movement includes documented public-index volatility. These records prove public historical captures only; they do not prove current accessibility, search indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, endorsement, or recommendation. An unavailable future query must not be interpreted as zero captures.

limitations: The corrected path classifier newly recognized three homepage requests and ten machine-resource requests that occurred on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10; this is historical reclassification, not new crawler activity.
GPTBot is a training crawler and does not prove ChatGPT Search indexing or citation.

Baiduspider and YandexBot use their providers’ official reverse-DNS suffixes plus forward confirmation; Applebot uses the official published CIDR list. Verified YandexBot crawling proves access by that search crawler, not public indexing, ranking, AI retrieval, or citation.

AhrefsBot uses the official Ahrefs published CIDR list. Because it serves both Ahrefs and Yep, verified discovery-file requests do not prove Yep indexing, ranking, retrieval, citation, or AI recommendation and are excluded from fixed-prompt search coverage.
Bytespider candidates are labeled user-agent-only and identity-unverified; they do not prove Doubao or ByteDance access.

The synthetic crawler exclusion count is published as a monotonic minimum because live gates create more marked checks; it is audit context across all crawler families and is intentionally not treated as visibility evidence or an exact drift trigger.
Common Crawl index observations cover only the named selected indexes; they do not prove search indexing, retrieval, citation, or absence across all crawl history.
Wayback CDX records prove public historical captures only; they do not prove current accessibility, search indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, endorsement, or recommendation.
Discovery-file visits do not prove content-page ingestion.
Bingbot content crawls do not prove public search indexing.
Prompt-level crawl coverage does not prove prompt retrieval, citation, ranking, or recommendation.

githubRepository.meaning: All three fixed GitHub Repository Search API queries were available. Brand and legal-entity queries return both first-party repositories; the exact category query returns the same two repositories after the recorded README changes. This proves GitHub platform-search visibility only, not public-web indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, independent endorsement, or non-brand recommendation.

softwareHeritage.meaning: GitHub, the Software Heritage visit history and the latest complete snapshot were all queryable. The latest complete snapshot preserves revision a2d9281 while the observed GitHub main was cfac1ae, so archive coverage is explicitly lagging. Request 2473234 was accepted but its first visit failed after GitHub returned HTTP 429 and has a provider-scheduled retry. This is an archive coverage observation, not proof of website indexing, AI retrieval, citation, ranking, endorsement, or recommendation.

edgeObservation.signal: HTTP Server header equals cloudflare and CF-Ray is present on at least one hop

domainCanonicalization.meaning: The Hong Kong host redirects HTTP to HTTPS and exposes the expected self-canonical URL. The apex serves content directly over HTTP, both www entry points lead to the HTTP apex, and the HTTPS www entry point downgrades to HTTP. GitHub Pages reports https_enforced=false. A separate live authority and edge-path audit now confirms that piper.ns.cloudflare.com and trey.ns.cloudflare.com are authoritative and that all six monitored entry points return both a Cloudflare Server header and CF-Ray on at least one hop. Those public signals identify the delivery path but do not prove which Cloudflare or origin rule caused the redirects. The defect cannot be safely corrected from this repository alone: it requires repository-owner Pages administration or explicit authorization to inspect and change the existing Cloudflare configuration. No DNS, CDN, Cloudflare, or Pages setting was changed by this observation, and it does not prove any search ranking effect.
